status: DESIGN ONLY - not run. Recommended verdict before running: STOP the LLM-as-selector line unless the gate experiment below finds residual (non-echo, non-score-following) choices that beat menu-random.

evidence_basis.this_workstream: O'Neil, k = 5..128, 117 calls: named replies with k >= 32 are verbatim prefixes of the presented order (9/9); with scores shown and order shuffled the reply re-sorts by displayed score (top-k overlap with presented order 0.49, with world-model top-k 0.77; Kendall tau vs model rank 0.66); blind replies reproduce the shuffled presented order (tau vs presented 1.0; world-model overlap 0.50 = chance)
evidence_basis.prior_receipts: dev_v2 (k = 15) agreement with world-model top-k 0.95 named / 0.94 anonymised / 0.50 blind; S6 blind - menu_random -0.17 [-0.71, 0.36]; S7 named - wm_full +0.05 [-0.05, 0.15]
evidence_basis.literature: Gupta et al. EMNLP 2025: permuted feedback labels do not change LLM-agent performance; classical BO beats LLM agents

gate_experiment.question: Does the LLM make any choice that is not explained by presentation order or displayed scores, and are those choices enriched for hits?
gate_experiment.data: O'Neil development (exposed; diagnostic only), all 39 lines, frozen campaign spec (10% budget, 4 rounds, k = 14-15, kappa 2)
gate_experiment.contract: frozen exact-k prompt at k <= 16 (one call per round), ids kept <= 3 digits (or positional codes 1..2k), presented order randomised per call with recorded seed, raw reply and presented order logged, failed calls priced at provider usage or reservation

arms.L_true: LLM, names + TRUE scores, shuffled order
arms.L_perm: LLM, names + scores PERMUTED across menu items, shuffled order (score-following control)
arms.R_sort: deterministic: sort the menu by displayed score (the rule L_true would follow if it only reads numbers) = wm top-k
arms.R_order: deterministic: take the first k of the presented order (= menu-random)

estimands: E2: hits(L_perm) - hits(R_order) per line (pharmacology/name knowledge net of the displayed numbers)
E3: share of picks not predicted by R_sort or R_order, and their hit rate vs the menu base rate
gate_experiment.calls_and_cost: 39 lines x 4 rounds x 2 LLM arms = 312 calls at about USD 0.0005 = about USD 0.16 (ceiling USD 0.30 incl. retries); one retry per invalid reply, charged and reported apart from first-attempt validity
gate_experiment.stop: STOP the LLM-as-selector line if the upper 95% bound of E1 and E2 (bootstrap over lines) is < +0.5 hits/line, or if > 90% of picks are predicted by R_sort/R_order
gate_experiment.continue: only if E2 > 0 with lower bound > 0 AND residual picks have a hit rate above the menu base rate; then run the full comparison below, preregistered, on a qualified untouched screen
gate_experiment.modify: if E1 ~ 0 but E2 > 0: use the LLM only to re-rank inside the world-model menu where it disagrees, with the certificate audit unchanged

arms: A0 random over all candidates (zero arm)
A2 strong deterministic agent WITHOUT the world model: retrieval + in-line drug-offset update from purchases (closed form, no learned variances)
A4 uniform choice from the world model's 2k menu (wm_menu_random) - the null for any within-menu planner
A5 LLM with world-model information (scores visible, order randomised)
A6 LLM with ablated model information: (a) scores withheld, (b) scores permuted, (c) drug names anonymised
A7 fallback/repair policy (LLM reply repaired from world-model order) reported as its OWN policy, never as LLM success
full_comparison_if_gate_passes.matching: identical 2k menus from the same world-model state; identical line evidence text; identical budget (experiments, dose points, wells, days) and round count; no arm may stop early unless all may, under the same rule; identical terminal audit and certificate
full_comparison_if_gate_passes.attribution: incremental contrasts A2-A1 (feedback without model), A3-A2 (model), A5-A3 (LLM beyond model), A6x-A4 (LLM knowledge net of model numbers), A7 vs A5 (repair); never only vs random
full_comparison_if_gate_passes.validity_gate: registered first-attempt exact-k validity >= 99% of calls on development at the evaluation screen's id format; otherwise the run is a protocol failure and no LLM contrast is reported
full_comparison_if_gate_passes.reporting: laboratory cost in wells/days per arm; provider USD, calls, tokens, latency and failures separately; unpriced failed calls bounded at reservation
full_comparison_if_gate_passes.inference: unit = target line; bootstrap over lines; LLM randomness: >= 2 seeds of presentation order per line; data scope: screens the model may have seen in pretraining (memorisation caveat stated)
full_comparison_if_gate_passes.data_prerequisite: a qualified untouched combination screen with the same label definition; ALMANAC is exposed and cannot serve as confirmation

worth_running: Gate only (USD ~0.16). The full comparison is not worth running on current evidence: the named planner's measurable degrees of freedom are presentation order and displayed scores, and the maximum effect is bounded by its disagreement with the world model (5-9% of picks at k = 15).
